scope: Durable routine creation and manual-run receipts, exact-request recovery, actual Pi final outcomes and initiating-session authorization in chat and workspace-management UI
skipped: Existing Linux-only file-descriptor race and dedicated UID checks on macOS.

behaviorEvidence.persistence: Actor/request-scoped receipts persist independently. Creation and receipt are one transaction; manual input, conversation timestamp, last/next run and receipt are one runtime transaction before dispatch. Identical accepted requests return the original receipt despite later edits, deletion or restart; mismatched payloads fail. Unaccepted manual requests require the exact observed editable configuration, excluding execution timestamps.
behaviorEvidence.runtime: Trusted manual entry fixes the intended Bot and binds the real initiating user/session rather than background owner authorization. Busy, maintenance and pending-human-input guards reject new dispatches before persistence. Actual Pi finalization records completion/error/cancellation/interruption with the original input and final assistant output. Intermediate tool turns do not count as task completion. Every assistant turn retains the trusted operation marker.
behaviorEvidence.recovery: Restart marks previously submitted runs interrupted and never dispatches them. Faults in terminal receipt persistence produce a conservative interrupted view, without replay. An explicit close request atomically returns an already-accepted receipt or tombstones an unaccepted ID. The commit transaction checks that tombstone again, preventing late posts even across SQLite connections. A lost close response can be resolved by a specific 410 response; no 404-based assumption releases the slot. Owner-only fixed-account HTTP GET/POST isolates receipts by user and workspace; authorization changes during commit roll back, and post-commit authorization loss does not falsely claim the request was not applied. App shutdown closes new operations before awaiting other service cleanup.
behaviorEvidence.ui: One pending intent per account/workspace in session storage contains only request ID, operation kind, optional routine ID and digest. Original request bodies exist only in the mounted page. Unknown responses offer read-only lookup and explicit same-payload retry after a missing result; remount without body cannot invent a retry. Storage refusal sends no request. Failed/late refresh cannot discard a confirmed receipt. Actual React handlers preserve editing drafts and protect navigation; chat and management use the same new operation flow without old-API fallback.
behaviorEvidence.navigation: Original task or message identity is verified before opening its conversation. History remains readable after deleting the source routine if the original input/conversation remain. The verification bootstrap is never installed over newer synchronization state. Stale account or workspace responses cannot navigate.

foundAndFixed: Review found a refresh with no original body and a missing receipt could leave new operations blocked indefinitely. Explicit transactional request closure now provides a safe exit and rejects late submissions, including across two SQLite connections.
The first synthetic Pi fixture asserted an intermediate done message before the next assistant turn began; the fixture was adjusted to stream the next turn explicitly.

The subsequent multi-turn run exposed production code dropping the operation marker on later assistant messages, preventing authoritative final receipt completion. Later turns now retain that marker; the actual Pi test passes.

Independent review found the new operation gate closed only after awaited app cleanup. It now closes at shutdown entry; an actual application test holds cleanup and verifies new operations are rejected.

desktopPackage.note: Existing native runtime and packaged archive remain byte-identical. No repackaging or new native GUI acceptance.

limitations: Product browser control still returns disabled; React event tests and controlled engine tests do not establish product visual/focus/touch acceptance.
The durable once-accepted request does not promise exactly-once external effects. Manual execution can perform real work; interrupted results require inspecting original chat and external state.

Legacy POST /routines and /routines/:id/run retain their prior semantics. New chat and workspace-management create/run paths exclusively use /routine-operations. Edit/pause/delete were not expanded into general durable operations.

Natural-language routine creation/editing, event triggers, recent run history, reference quotas/deletion confirmation and other multi-device/full-reference gaps remain recorded; original goal stays active.
